title: Brother's claim to a compassionate job

scenes.dialogue: A driver with a State bus corporation dies in service. His wife had died before him, and there were no children. Can his brother now get a job on compassionate grounds?
His mother sought a job for her other son, who promised to look after her. The corporation said no, but a single judge of the Karnataka High Court said yes.

scenes.dialogue: The corporation's rule covers a married employee's widow and children. A brother qualifies only if the employee was unmarried. So it rejected the claim.
The single judge held that when the wife died first and there are no children, mere marriage cannot bar the claim, and ordered the corporation to appoint him within twelve weeks.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? Marriage is a fact in an employee's life, and a wife's death does not erase it. A widower is not an unmarried man.
A promise to look after the mother cannot create eligibility. So the appeal was allowed, and the corporation's rejection was upheld.
